thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: auth-service — sudden spike in 401s and token-reuse signatures. Window: 5m; total 401s=5600; top source CIDRs: 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.45. Possible staging log forwarder leaked auth headers to s3. Marking P1.

jen (oncall): ack. i'm on pager. sam, please take lead for immediate mitigation. maria looped for sec/forensics. carol, please standby for cust comm triage. :white_check_mark:

sam (sre): looking. pulling recent log-forwarder activity. quick grep: ```
$ aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket staging-logs --prefix logger/2026-03-01
...
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ingest-9f3a...
user=svc-ingest-prod id=svc-ingest-9f3a env=staging
```
We have plain `Authorization` headers in forwarded payloads for a subset of staging streams. That matches the token pattern. Initial hypothesis: a config change in log-forwarder allowed raw headers to be included in the payload sent to the s3 target.

sam (sre): mitigation plan (short): 1) revoke exposed ingest token 2) hotpatch forwarder to strip `Authorization` header 3) block suspicious source CIDRs at edge 4) assess customer impact + notify. Doing 1 now.

sam (sre): running revoke: ```sh
$ redwoodctl auth revoke --token sk-prod-ingest-9f3a
> 200 OK - token revoked
```
sam (sre): revoke returned OK. rotating replacement token and updating our ingest fleet via config rollout (canary first).

maria (sec): good. please snapshot the implicated s3 objects and preserve for forensics (do not delete). also remove public ACL and tighten bucket policy ASAP. tagging legal for retention policy.

carol (support): checking customer impact. early signals: a small number of customers saw increased 401s when ingest switched to the rotated token. one support ticket (T-10672) reports repeated 401s for webhook uploads starting ~10:02 UTC. I'm ready to send an initial acknowledgement once we confirm timeline.

legal-team: noted. preserve logs and metadata. legal requests we do not purge or alter original objects until we complete preliminary review. please set object lock on the snapshot.

sam (sre): hotpatch to forwarder done — added header scrub and config validation. rollout id: rollout-20260301-a. quick command used: ```yaml
forwarder.config:
  strip_headers: [Authorization, X-Internal-Token]
  validate_targets: [s3-staging, s3-archive]
```
Applied to canary hosts (5), monitoring for error rate.

jen (oncall): edge firewall rule in progress to block 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.45 for auth endpoints. sam, what's ETA for full fleet token swap?

sam (sre): canaries ok. full swap rolling, ETA ~22 minutes. updating rollout dashboard. I've also kicked off a background scan for tokens in other recent s3 uploads: `s3grep --pattern "Authorization: Bearer" --since 2026-02-28`.

maria (sec): Maria here — once swap complete, start KMS key rotation for the auditshipper bucket (we suspect config drift allowed header passthrough). coordinate with infra. Also open a GH issue to add CI check preventing forwarder configs with `strip_headers` unset.

carol (support): drafting customer note: "We detected and contained an issue where forwarding configuration allowed auth headers to be stored in staging logs. We have revoked the affected token, stripped headers, and are investigating scope. No evidence of exfiltration to external parties at this time. We'll follow up with timeline and remediation steps." Want legal to review before posting.

legal-team: reviewing. hold on posting until we confirm affected customer list. request list of buckets/object keys and timestamps for preservation.

sam (sre): scan results (prelim): found 14 object keys (staging-logger/*/2026-03-01T10:00Z) with Authorization header present. Exporting list to secure bucket `forensics-snapshots/2098765432/`.

jen (oncall): good work. next steps: 1) complete rollout and confirm 401s resolved 2) finalize customer impacted list 3) legal review 4) schedule postmortem + followups (CI guardrails, bucket policy hardening, KMS rotate). tagging owners. anyone else? :mag: 

carol (support): will update T-10672 and begin templated outreach once legal gives the ok. also will prepare status page blurb (ops.redwood.ai/status) in staging.

maria (sec): paging sec-oncall for deep forensics and long-term retention decision. Also recommend rotating any service principals that used the exposed token.

sam (sre): rollout complete. monitoring shows auth error rate back to baseline. quick grep: 401 spike flattened around 10:18 UTC.

pagerbot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE: token revoked, forwarder hotpatched, firewall rules applied, canary->full rollout complete. Forensics snapshot stored at s3://forensics-snapshots/2098765432/.

jen (oncall): handing off to ops and sec for post-incident work. I'll create the postmortem ticket and invite relevant parties. handing to oncall rotation tomorrow. Thanks team.

carol (support): will queue customer comm after legal review.

legal-team: confirm review complete; OK to send the drafted customer message with minor language tweaks. preserving snapshot per retention policy.

sam (sre): note for followups: add automated ci job to lint forwarder configs, add unit test to strip sensitive headers by default, and add a regression eval for s3 ACL changes.

maria (sec): opened forensics ticket INC-FOR-2098765432 and assigned sec engineers.

jen (oncall): closing the live pager thread. leaving the channel for postmortem coordination. :lock:
